body: cc @annevk as a standalone PR this looks good to me and fixes some of the issues I ran into in the spec. Not sure about the underlying PR.
Since it builds on https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13188 someone will have to address the comments there first.
Huh actually I think the stacking UI confused me and this is the bottom of the stack?

<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 39bc5a4. Lint and build pass. The tree scoping (shadow trees, both sides of ID removals and cross-tree ID moves) and the ID-change condition in the attribute change steps check out against DOM's ID update steps.

I pushed 4f100a6 with editorial fixes: the helper takes a node rather than "a root", "non-empty", and the note now also mentions custom element upgrades.

**Blockers**

- In the [removing steps](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/39bc5a447381cba101f784b36a04f2447fdc3074/source#L1867-L1878), the detached side is only reset when an element with an ID is removed. Take a connected `<div>` with `innerHTML = "<form><input form=missing></form>"`, so `input.form` is null. After `div.remove()`, nothing resets the input: its owner is null and nothing removed has an ID, so it stays null. If the `<form>` has any unrelated `id`, though, the *removedNode*'s-root reset runs and the input falls back to its ancestor form, per step 5 of *reset the form owner*. Chromium (`ListedElement::RemovedFrom`) and WebKit (`FormListedElement::elementRemovedFromAncestor`) reset every form-attribute control that gets disconnected, so both give the form in either case. Gecko gives null, but only because it never falls back to an ancestor for a control with a `form` attribute (`UpdateFormOwner`), which contradicts step 5. Consider a step "If *removedNode* is a listed form-associated element with a `form` attribute and *oldAncestor* is connected, then reset the form owner of *removedNode*", which makes the *removedNode*'s-root sub-step unnecessary. This also needs a WPT and a Gecko bug.
- In the [moving steps](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/39bc5a447381cba101f784b36a04f2447fdc3074/source#L1899-L1916), a cross-tree move of a form-attribute control without an ID isn't covered. With `<input form=f>` in a shadow root and `<form id=f>` in the document, `document.body.moveBefore(input, null)` leaves `input.form` null. The input's owner was null and it has no ID, so neither step applies. Chromium (`ListedElement::InsertedInto`) and, per #13185, Firefox reset the form owner on moves and end up with `f`. Consider also resetting *movedNode* when it is a listed control with a `form` attribute and *oldAncestor*'s root differs from its root. Or pull in the unconditional "If *movedNode* is a form-associated element, then reset the form owner" from your #13185 draft, which also fixes same-tree moves from one form to another. This needs a WPT too.

**Suggestions**

- Consider moving "[These run after the attribute change steps that update *element*'s ID](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/39bc5a447381cba101f784b36a04f2447fdc3074/source#L1921-L1926)" into DOM. DOM doesn't order hook definitions, so this is a cross-spec ordering requirement that DOM doesn't currently provide. A small DOM change could update the ID in *handle attribute changes* before the attribute change steps run (or make the ID derived, per #10331), and then this sentence can go.
- The `connected` guards are inconsistent. [Insertion](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/39bc5a447381cba101f784b36a04f2447fdc3074/source#L1808-L1810) and [removing](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/39bc5a447381cba101f784b36a04f2447fdc3074/source#L1868-L1869) check `connected`; moving and attribute change don't. Today the guards only matter because they keep the stale owner from the first blocker. In the detached `<div>` from that example, appending a `<span id=z>` leaves the input at null, while setting `id` on an element already inside it resets the input to the form. Once that blocker is fixed, a disconnected form-attribute control's owner never depends on IDs. Consider a single "If *root* is not connected, then return" in the helper instead of the per-hook guards.

**Nits**

- Consider having [the helper](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/39bc5a447381cba101f784b36a04f2447fdc3074/source#L61152-L61166) take the affected ID(s) and reset only controls whose `form` value matches, which is how all three engines key their form-attribute observers. Once the blockers are fixed this is unobservable, and it avoids a full-tree walk for every inserted element with an ID.
- In the PR body, #1571 was closed as a duplicate of #10331, so "Helps with #1571" can go. The "Matches all existing browsers" entry needs updating for the two blockers.

</details>

Both blockers fixed, and tests and Gecko bug created.

Fixed DOM with https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/1525, which ideally should merge first (but in practice it's pretty obvious what the intended ordering is so I wouldn't make it a strict blocker).

GPT-6 Astra High says

> Moving: added the narrow cross-tree reset. I avoided unconditional resets, which would pull same-tree moves and parser-established associations into this PR.

which is related to the general fact that the ordering between this and @lukewarlow's work is a bit unclear, at least to me. My intention was to do everything not related to custom elements in my PRs and leave custom elements to @lukewarlow but of course everything is entangled, so I'm not sure if that plan is working well.

Note that this is indeed the bottom of the stack with https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13188 being on top.

Fwiw I think this being merged first (or after) works for my stuff I've tried to layer things independently enough that it's easy to rebase either way.

Ultimately there's a lot to fix and I don't think doing it in one big PR is actually the right move for this.

Apparently 

> The ID attribute change steps could be simplified because reset the form owner with a form attribute already takes care of the relevant filtering.

isn't quite right. The extra calls to "reset the form owner" would, per the current spec and Gecko behavior, temporarily set the form owner to null, and then set it back. This has effects on radio group stuff.

I'll push a commit to match Blink/WebKit, for which "reset the form owner" does nothing if the new owner equals the old owner. Plus WPTs and a second Gecko bug.

Oh dear. I'm not sure what to do now. All browsers have the WebKit behavior on removal (at least for radio groups.) That means my latest pushed commit matches no browsers.

I guess we could spec the Chromium/WebKit behavior, which apparently does an extra step to clear the form owner? Maybe there was some reason for that?

Source links, with a correction: the two engines reach the temporary null owner differently.

- WebKit explicitly calls [`setForm(nullptr)` immediately before `resetFormOwner()`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/358a8c23a999e320c2b58f5ded3f12f72b6d2973/Source/WebCore/html/FormListedElement.cpp#L85-L95) when disconnecting a control with a `form` attribute.
- Chromium instead [notifies ID observers when removing the form's ID](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c26b6c74cca6a05e247f11e3d56ceb229aff39ce/third_party/blink/renderer/core/dom/tree_scope.cc#L157-L165). Removal notifications [visit ancestors before descendants](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c26b6c74cca6a05e247f11e3d56ceb229aff39ce/third_party/blink/renderer/core/dom/container_node.cc#L1423-L1437), so the control still has its connected flag: the observer-triggered reset [looks up the now-missing ID and sets the owner to null](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c26b6c74cca6a05e247f11e3d56ceb229aff39ce/third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/listed_element.cc#L394-L420). The control's own [removal hook resets it again](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c26b6c74cca6a05e247f11e3d56ceb229aff39ce/third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/listed_element.cc#L232-L236), this time restoring the ancestor form. There is no equivalent explicit pre-reset clear in that hook.

> That's a nice find. While reviewing your latest change I found a problem with WebKit setting form to null eagerly on removal before calling reset form owner.

I found a case where WebKit was setting formOwner to null and then never even resetting it too... https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=331116 (I think FIrefox has the same bug on that one too) Not sure if these are related cases or not.

Alright, updated WPTs to match this more-sensible model, where disconnecting a form cannot uncheck unrelated radios, and filed bugs on all 3 browsers. Per discussions in Matrix, WebKit is interested. Anyone from Gecko or Chromium want to chime in to support this edge-case fix?? @noamr @smaug----
